question.text: In Convertible Arbitrage the COUPON INTEREST on the convertible bond is economically:

answer.text: A cost that offsets the arb spread.
An additional income (quasi risk-free) that partly funds the short leg's borrow fees and dividend forgone.
Payable to the equity short counterparty.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 10.1.3 explicit: coupon interest is an ADDITIONAL risk-free income for the fund, which helps offset short-leg borrow fees and dividends forgone. It is a key carry component of convertible arb. The Trap: Option A inverts the role of coupon by calling it a cost. Option C fabricates a payment to the equity short counterparty. Option D incorrectly tags Section 194LBB pass-through, which applies to Cat I/II — Cat III is taxed at the fund level. Note: Coupon, borrow fees, and dividends forgone are the three carry components in the workbook's convertible-arbitrage example; coupon supports the long convertible position while borrow fees and dividends forgone are the cost of the short leg.
